module_role: EtherCAT defines two distinct silicon roles with different integration profiles. (1) The EtherCAT SubDevice (Slave) integrates an EtherCAT Slave Controller (ESC) — usually 2-4 Ethernet ports + on-the-fly engine + FMMU + SyncManager + DPRAM + DC + SII + PDI — alongside a local application µC running the slave stack and the application's I/O logic. (2) The MainDevice (Master) uses a standard PC or industrial controller with any commodity Ethernet NIC; no EtherCAT-specific silicon is required on the controller side. The slave stack is the focus of most EtherCAT IP cores and integration documentation.
topology_description: Daisy-chain (line) is the canonical topology: MainDevice → SubDevice₁ Port 0 → Port 1 → SubDevice₂ Port 0 → Port 1 → ... → SubDevice_N. Each SubDevice ESC has hardware auto-loopback on any port without an active link partner, so the frame physically traverses every device twice on the same cable run (once outbound, once returning), creating one logical bus. Tree topologies are formed by using SubDevices with 3 or 4 ports (e.g., EK1100, ET1815). Ring topology with cable redundancy uses two MainDevice NICs and closes the cable loop. Drop-line topology is a tree branch terminated by a stub. Mixed combinations of line / tree / star / ring are supported.
integration_overview: A typical SubDevice ASIC integration: ESC IP (Beckhoff ET1100/ET1200/ET1815 ASIC, Microchip LAN9252, or FPGA IP from Intel/Xilinx/Lattice) is placed between the Ethernet PHYs and the application µC. The ESC's Ethernet ports connect via MII/RMII/RGMII to two (or more) integrated 10/100 Ethernet PHYs (e.g. Microchip LAN8710, TI DP83822). The PHYs drive 100BASE-TX magnetics + RJ-45 jacks (or M8/M12 industrial connectors). The ESC's PDI connects to the application µC's external bus / SPI; the µC runs the slave stack (state-machine, mailbox protocol handlers, application-specific I/O code). An external SII EEPROM (1-32 Kbit typical) holds the ESI XML descriptor. SYNC0/SYNC1 outputs from the ESC drive the µC's cycle interrupt for time-synchronized I/O.

interfaces: 100BASE-TX over Cat 5 / Cat 5e UTP with RJ-45 or M8/M12 industrial connector
EtherCAT P: 100BASE-TX + 2 × 24 V power on same cable
Digital I/O (up to 32-bit in + 32-bit out, no µC needed)
On-chip CPU bus (AMBA AHB / AXI / Avalon-MM) for ASIC integration
I²C-compatible 2-wire to serial EEPROM (1 Kbit-4 Mbit)
PDI emulation (µC supplies SII content, bit 8 of 0x0500 set)
SYNC0 / SYNC1 — output pulses to local µC, programmable period in 0x0990 / 0x0994
LATCH0 / LATCH1 — external event inputs that capture System Time
RUN (ESM state), ERR (AL error), LINK (PHY link), ACT (TX/RX activity) per port

interconnect_topologies_supported.name: Tree
interconnect_topologies_supported.description: Junctions formed by SubDevices with 3 or 4 ports; allows physical fan-out.

interconnect_topologies_supported.name: Star
interconnect_topologies_supported.description: All branches off one central SubDevice with many ports.

interconnect_topologies_supported.name: Ring
interconnect_topologies_supported.description: Two MainDevice NICs close the cable loop; on cable break the segment auto-divides into two healthy line segments.

interconnect_topologies_supported.name: Drop line
interconnect_topologies_supported.description: Tree branches terminating in a stub device.

interconnect_topologies_supported.name: Hot Connect / Hot Swap
interconnect_topologies_supported.description: Groups of SubDevices may be added or removed during operation; MainDevice tolerates absence.

default_signal_values_when_omitted.default_when_unused: Each port that is not connected loops back internally via DL Control 0x0100

soc_dependent_items: PHY choice (Microchip LAN8710 / TI DP83822 / Marvell 88E1111 / Realtek RTL8201 etc.) — vendor-specific MDIO register quirks
Magnetics + connector mechanicals (RJ-45 / M8 / M12 / M23)
PDI bus electrical levels (3.3 V vs 5 V µC interfacing)
External SII EEPROM choice + capacity (1 Kbit / 4 Kbit / 32 Kbit / 1 Mbit)
Application µC class (8-bit / 16-bit / 32-bit Cortex-M / FPGA NIOS / RISC-V) — determines slave-stack performance ceiling

key_elements: Mailbox protocols supported bitmask (CoE / SoE / EoE / FoE / AoE / VoE)
CoE Object Dictionary skeleton (for diagnostic discovery)
